envelope.mechanism: host-side warden aggregate envelope + sized tmpfs storage + per-process rlimits (cgroup v2 unavailable on this host)

cgroup.reason: cgroup v2 limit files absent in a fresh child cgroup (missing: memory.max, cpu.max, pids.max); the visible hierarchy's cgroup.controllers is empty, so no memory/cpu/pids controller is available to delegate

aggregate.mechanism: host-side warden: /proc census of the room's pid namespace every 0.05s

memory.rule: sustained at working, immediate at catastrophic
memory.measure: summed RSS of the processes the census observes. This is NOT total host memory charged to the room: tmpfs pages are bounded separately by the storage ceiling, and other kernel-side allocations are not inside the RSS sum.

pids.rule: sustained at working, immediate at catastrophic

cpu.boundary: per worker run: executions are serialised by a per-room lock, and the budget is cumulative across all calls in the run (run ledger in this state)
cpu.contract: the CPU limit is a cumulative accounting budget, not a hard execution ceiling — in-flight enforcement acts on what the census observes; work that completes between observations can exceed the budget; the excess is charged exactly and further calls are refused
cpu.rule: cumulative accounting across the run's calls; in flight the warden trips when the census-observed run total crosses the budget; a call that starts with the budget spent is refused before execution; work that completes between observations can exceed the budget and is charged exactly at call end, with further calls refused
cpu.accounting: in flight: the warden's census level (each observed process's own + reaped-children CPU from /proc stat). Per call: reconciled with the in-room reaper's exact collected rusage; the ledger is charged the larger of the two.

aggregate.granularity: poll-based userspace enforcement: a breach is detected at the first census after it forms (and, for the working ceiling, after the sustain window); overshoot is bounded by consumption during one poll interval plus, for sustained kills, the sustain window — measured figures are recorded per execution, not guaranteed bounds

storage.identity_note: the mount identity (mount id + device) and size recorded here are re-verified against the LIVE mount table at every execution (Room._verify_storage_live); the recorded label alone never authorises a run
storage.enforcement: kernel: writes past the tmpfs size fail with ENOSPC; the ceiling is aggregate over the whole tree
storage.loop_image_evaluated: fixed-size image + loop mount is unavailable on this host: no /dev/loop* devices exist (losetup cannot find an unused loop device)

per_process_rlimits.caveat: second layer only: per-process (NPROC per room uid), inherited — NOT the room envelope

storage.enforcement: kernel: writes past the tmpfs size fail with ENOSPC; the ceiling is aggregate over the whole tree
storage.loop_image_evaluated: fixed-size image + loop mount is unavailable on this host: no /dev/loop* devices exist (losetup cannot find an unused loop device)

persistence.filesystem_state: persists across calls within a run — one tree per room, bind-mounted into every execution
persistence.process_state: does not persist — every execution is a fresh process tree in a fresh pid namespace; no process survives the end of its own call
persistence.interpreter_state: does not persist — no interpreter or shell session is held between calls; only files carry state between calls

envelope_boundary: per worker run: executions serialised by a per-room lock; instantaneous ceilings apply to the room's one running execution; the CPU budget is cumulative across the run's calls (cpu_ledger)

cpu_ledger.contract: the CPU limit is a cumulative accounting budget, not a hard execution ceiling — in-flight enforcement acts on what the census observes; work that completes between observations can exceed the budget; the excess is charged exactly and further calls are refused

import hashlib, json, os, sys
out = {"cwd": os.getcwd()}
ok = True
hashes = {}
for rel in sys.argv[1:4]:
    try:
        with open(rel, "rb") as fh:
            hashes[rel] = hashlib.sha256(fh.read()).hexdigest()
    except OSError as exc:
        hashes[rel] = f"ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        ok = False
out["source_hashes"] = hashes
token = sys.argv[4]
try:
    probe = "/room/scratch/.smoke-write-probe"
    with open(probe, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(token)
    with open(probe) as fh:
        back = fh.read()
    os.unlink(probe)
    out["scratch_write_readback"] = (back == token)
    ok = ok and (back == token)
except OSError as exc:
    out["scratch_write_readback"] = f"ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    ok = False
try:
    with open(sys.argv[5], "w") as fh:
        fh.write("stocking smoke probe - not the deliverable\n")
    out["deliverable_writable"] = os.path.exists(sys.argv[5])
    ok = ok and out["deliverable_writable"]
except OSError as exc:
    out["deliverable_writable"] = f"ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    ok = False
print(json.dumps(out))
sys.exit(0 if ok else 3)
